description: Monotonic descending sweep of feed-forward widths below the retained 44-wide bottleneck, one candidate per runner-mediated micro-trial.
proposal: Family: feed-forward width. Retained incumbent is 5824 parameters at 99.950000%, a +0.950000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: accepted attempt-0002 at ff=44 (5824, 99.95%); no scored failure; 1 prior attempt. Hypothesis: the retained 44-wide bottleneck may tolerate further four-channel decrements while learned positional embeddings and attention remain fixed. This is a parameterization-preserving compression, not a representational change. Ordering: test ff widths 40, 36, 32, 28, 24, 20 in descending order, always from the retained source. Acceptance/rollback: the runner retains only a qualified strictly smaller candidate and otherwise restores the incumbent; after any scored discard or error, stop because the monotonic smaller-width branch is ineligible until a different mechanism changes the hypothesis. Stopping: first discard/error, no eligible widths, or six micro-trials. Maximum micro-trials: 6. Compute budget: at most 180000 training steps and six runner training windows (21600 seconds configured maximum); no train, verify, retain, or discard action occurs outside the runner. This is more informative than jumping directly to ff=32 because it resolves the nearest untested capacity boundary.
summary: Tested feed-forward widths 40, 36, 32, 28, 24, and 20 in descending order. All six micro-trials qualified and were retained; the final frontier is ff=20 with 4288 parameters and 99.910000% official development-verifier accuracy. There were no scored failures or errors. Compute used: 6 x 30000 = 180000 training steps, about 52 minutes wall-clock from the archived micro-trial timestamps. Stopped because the declared six-micro-trial cap was reached, as recorded by AUTOMATION_TRIGGER.json.
